In July 2022, Apple reported an 11% decline in Q3 profits compared to 2021. Its revenue in the same period rose 2% year-on-year to $83 billion, though this figure was also lower than in 2021, where the increase was at 36%. The general downturn is reportedly caused by the slowing global economy and supply chain disruptions in China.[304]

Apple amassed 65% of all profits made by the eight largest worldwide smartphone manufacturers in quarter one of 2014, according to a report by Canaccord Genuity. In the first quarter of 2015, the company garnered 92% of all earnings.[298]

- **Historical Leadership**: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft and served as CEO for many years, remains involved as a board member and significant shareholder
- **Governance**: Standard public company structure with professional management

## **Alphabet Inc. (Google's Parent Company)**
- **Major Owners**: Larry Page and Sergey Brin (Google co-founders) remain controlling shareholders
- **Current CEO**: Sundar Pichai (CEO of both Google and Alphabet)
- **Structure**: Alphabet is the parent company that owns Google and other subsidiaries
- **Leadership**: While Page and Brin stepped down from day-to-day executive roles in 2019, they maintain significant control through their share holdings

- **Microsoft** has transitioned from founder control to professional management
- **Alphabet/Google** maintains founder control through Page and Brin's shareholdings despite stepping back from operational roles

All of these companies are publicly traded on stock exchanges (primarily NASDAQ), meaning ownership is distributed among millions of shareholders, but in some cases, founders maintain controlling interests through special share classes or large personal holdings.
